feature: Current ATSC editions and the editions adopted nationally

ATSC.page: A/321 p.ii; A/322 pp.ii–iii; change summary pp.3–5
ATSC.value: Current published ATSC baseline: 11 June 2026. It includes the 2022 Time Expression clarification, 2024 MIMO/LDM/channel-bonding extensions, 2025 errata, January 2026 pilot correction and June 2026 bootstrap clarification. This is not the US regulatory incorporation baseline.

TTA.value: References A/321 (2016.03), A/322 (2020.01) and A/324 CS (2020.01). Selected later corrections and Layered MIMO text are present, but parity-interleaver, time-example and MIMO-table differences remain. Appendix I-1 explicitly says it is not part of the standard.
TTA.req: national standard body; appendix status must be distinguished

SBTVD.doc: Anatel Ato 2.705/2026 · ABNT NBR 25601:2025 · SBTVD OG-01 (Jan 2026)
SBTVD.value: Transmitter/retransmitter rule references A/321:2025-07, A/322:2025-07a and A/324:2025-07. OG-01 already prohibits MP4_2 with 32K FFT. The non-normative guideline and the ABNT normative profile are separate evidence layers.
SBTVD.req: transmitter rule mandatory; OG-01 non-normative; ABNT profile not fully verified

difference: Both countries use earlier cited editions than the current ATSC baseline. The Korean differences are not limited to the two 2026 changes. Brazil has an older regulatory reference and a newer operating guideline addressing the MP4_2 issue.
impact: A common technology baseline does not establish complete clause identity or equipment interoperability. US A/322:2017 incorporation applies to at least one free primary video stream; it is not a mandate to implement the latest edition.

TTA.text: Later content is mixed into the 2020 reference basis; confirmed equation, time and MIMO-table differences remain.

SBTVD.text: Ato edition references verified; OG-01 mitigates the known pilot issue; the complete ABNT profile remains unverified.

evidence.label: TTA Part 4 — references and inspected clauses

recommendation: Track cited edition, technical deltas, normative status and implementation evidence separately. Retain the original TTA wording and propose explicit errata rather than silently treating it as current ATSC text.

feature: Bootstrap waveform dimensions and major-version-0 symbol count

ATSC.value: 6.144 Ms/s; 4.5 MHz; FFT 2048; 3 kHz spacing; 500 µs per symbol; ZC sequence modulated by PN. For major version 0, N_S is at least 4.
ATSC.req: normative waveform dimensions; symbol-count statement scoped to major version 0

TTA.value: The inspected dimensions and major-version-0 structure match the current ATSC values. This finding does not cover the new major-version-1 or heterogeneous-frame clauses.
TTA.req: normative body provisions for the defined waveform

SBTVD.doc: A/321:2025-07 by Ato reference · SBTVD OG-01
SBTVD.value: The referenced ATSC waveform has the same listed dimensions; OG-01 describes a 4.5 MHz, 2K-FFT bootstrap. ABNT profile not fully verified.
SBTVD.req: Ato requirement for transmitters/retransmitters; OG-01 non-normative

difference: No difference found in these explicitly listed major-version-0 waveform dimensions. Document-level or national-profile identity is not inferred.
impact: The compared acquisition waveform is common. Actual receiver acquisition and interoperability have not been tested.

TTA.text: Inspected dimensions and major-version-0 symbol-count rule match.

SBTVD.text: Referenced dimensions and OG-01 waveform description match; complete ABNT profile not verified.

recommendation: Keep the numerical finding scoped to the listed dimensions and major version 0.

feature: Major-version-0 signaling and current heterogeneous-waveform provisions

ATSC.value: Major 0 uses ZC root 137; symbol 1 carries EA bit 1, min_time_to_next (5 bits) and bandwidth; symbol 2 carries EA bit 2 and bsr_coefficient (0–80); symbol 3 carries preamble_structure. Bandwidth 11 means greater than 8 MHz. ATSC 3.0 constrains major/minor to 0 and coefficients to 2/5/8 for 6/7/8 MHz. Current A/321 also defines root 197 for major 1, future roots and bootstrap-prefixed heterogeneous frames.
ATSC.req: normative ATSC 3.0 constraints; heterogeneous-frame clauses have their own scope

TTA.value: Major-version-0 fields and the MIMO/Layered-MIMO bootstrap-amplitude rule are present. Current A/321 §§6.2–6.3 and 7 have no counterpart in the inspected Part 4 text.
TTA.req: major-version-0 body provisions; no adoption identified for the current added clauses

SBTVD.value: Ato cites the earlier edition; OG-01 describes version-0 operation. The 2026 heterogeneous-frame clarification is not in the cited edition. Full ABNT profile unverified.
SBTVD.req: Ato transmitter requirement; OG-01 non-normative guidance

difference: Major-version-0 fields match in the inspected texts. The current ATSC document additionally covers other version roots and requires a bootstrap before every frame when signal types share an RF channel.
impact: The added clauses are relevant when heterogeneous physical-layer waveforms share the channel. No operational mixed-waveform transmission or legacy-receiver behavior was tested.

TTA.text: Version-0 fields match; current §§6.2–6.3 and 7 are absent from the inspected national text.

SBTVD.text: Earlier referenced edition and version-0 guidance verified; current added clauses and ABNT profile are not fully matched.

recommendation: Show a scoped match for major version 0 and a separate partial match for the complete current document; do not label all 2026 additions irrelevant without stating the operating condition.

feature: Channel bandwidth, sample rate and number of carriers

ATSC.value: ATSC 3.0 defines 6/7/8 MHz operation. NoC_max is 6913/13825/27649 for 8K/16K/32K; C_unit is 96/192/384 and C_red_coeff is 0–4. General bootstrap sample-rate signaling is (N+16)×0.384 MHz; ATSC coefficients are 2, 5 and 8 respectively.
ATSC.req: defined technical options; market/channel rules are separate

TTA.value: Listed NoC values match. The cited national rule specifies 6 MHz channels and occupied bandwidth no greater than 6 MHz.
TTA.req: 6 MHz under the cited national rule

SBTVD.clause: Decreto Art.2 III; Ato §4.1; OG-01 §5.1 Tables 1–2
SBTVD.value: Decreto defines a 6 MHz RF channel. OG-01 reproduces coefficients 2/5/8 and the NoC table but defers channel operation to local regulations. Full ABNT receiver profile unverified.
SBTVD.req: 6 MHz decree definition; transmitter rule; OG-01 non-normative

difference: The listed parameters use the same ATSC options. Korea and Brazil select 6 MHz within the cited regulatory scope; ATSC also defines 7 and 8 MHz.
impact: Domestic services in the cited scope use the 6 MHz signaling values. This comparison alone does not establish every receiver hardware-support obligation or exclude other territories and test settings.

TTA.text: Listed carrier parameters match; 6 MHz is a defined ATSC option selected by the cited rule.

SBTVD.text: Decree channel definition and inspected OG-01 coefficients/carrier table match the defined 6 MHz option; ABNT receiver obligations remain separate.

recommendation: Retain the regulation scope and distinguish the general bootstrap formula from the restricted ATSC coefficient set.

feature: SISO FFT sizes, guard intervals and pilot-pattern options

ATSC.value: 8K/16K/32K FFT; 12 guard-interval patterns (192–4864 samples), subject to allowed combinations; 16 SISO scattered-pilot patterns. Annex D specifies continual pilots and Annex E scattered pilots; Annex F is boundary-symbol data cells and Annex G tone-reservation carriers.
ATSC.req: normative available waveform options; selected-mode obligations must be scoped

TTA.value: The listed FFT/GI/SISO pattern options correspond to ATSC. Appendix I-1 has an explicit not-part-of-the-standard declaration. All carrier-index arrays were not independently recomputed.

SBTVD.value: OG-01 gives FFT operating recommendations and pilot constraints, including the 32K MP4_2 exclusion for MIMO. The complete ABNT normative operating/receiver profile has not been verified.

difference: The listed SISO options correspond. Text-similarity scores do not establish exact equality of all pilot tables or carrier positions. MIMO-specific differences are recorded separately.
impact: Choice of FFT, GI and pilot settings affects service robustness and payload. No operational profile or receiver performance was measured.

TTA.text: Listed SISO FFT/GI/pilot options correspond; no claim of a complete carrier-index audit.

SBTVD.text: Referenced options and OG-01 recommendations identified; full ABNT normative profile not verified.

recommendation: Use Annex D/E for pilot references and distinguish the inspected option list from unverified numeric arrays and national support profiles.

feature: FEC length/rate and constellation options (not full BICM identity)

ATSC.value: LDPC lengths 16200/64800, twelve rates 2/15–13/15; outer BCH (168/192 parity bits), CRC-32 or none; QPSK and non-uniform 16/64/256/1024/4096 QAM. Not every length/rate/modulation combination is allowed.
ATSC.req: defined coding/modulation options; mode-combination constraints apply

TTA.value: The listed FEC and constellation option sets correspond. A distinct parity-interleaver endpoint discrepancy exists in §6.2.1 and is recorded in phy-parity-interleaver; therefore the complete BICM chapter is not identical.
TTA.req: body options; cited rule allows LDPC+BCH, LDPC+CRC32 or LDPC and QAM including QPSK

SBTVD.value: The same coding/modulation toolbox is referenced. OG-01 explicitly distinguishes required modulation/code-rate combinations from the whole available set. Full ABNT normative requirements remain unverified.
SBTVD.req: transmitter rule; OG-01 non-normative; required combination profile needs ABNT verification

difference: The listed technology options correspond. This is not a finding that every BICM equation, interleaver or coefficient table is identical, nor that every receiver must support every option.
impact: Selected-mode interoperability requires correct interleavers and permitted combinations in addition to matching the high-level FEC/constellation names.

TTA.text: Listed FEC/constellation options correspond; complete BICM identity is explicitly excluded.

SBTVD.text: Toolbox is referenced; OG-01 defines a subset distinction and ABNT normative requirements remain unverified.

recommendation: Keep this row scoped to options and consult the separate parity discrepancy and national combination profiles before making a full conformance claim.

ATSC.value: The parity mapping uses 0 ≤ s < 360 and 0 ≤ t < Q_ldpc; the output vector has N_inner entries.
ATSC.req: normative equation for Type B codes

TTA.value: The printed equation uses 0 ≤ s ≤ 360. This inclusive endpoint differs from current ATSC and exceeds the declared vector range at the last t. The PDF glyph was visually checked.
TTA.req: printed body equation differs; proposed erratum, not an edited national standard

SBTVD.value: The ATSC technical equation is incorporated through the cited edition. No Brazil-specific parity-endpoint alteration was identified in the reviewed OG-01; complete ABNT text remains unverified.
SBTVD.req: transmitter reference requirement; national profile not fully verified

difference: Korean s=360 with t=Q_ldpc−1 addresses output u[N_inner] and input lambda[N_inner+Q_ldpc−1], outside a length-N_inner vector. This is a printed-equation discrepancy, not observed equipment behavior.
impact: A literal implementation of the extra endpoint would be invalid. Actual encoders/decoders may implement the intended ATSC equation; their behavior has not been tested.
recommendation: Record a Korean erratum proposal replacing the upper ≤ with < and verify implementations separately. Do not retain a full BICM Same verdict while this difference is open.

TTA.text: Confirmed printed endpoint discrepancy: ≤360 versus current ATSC <360.

SBTVD.text: ATSC equation is referenced; complete ABNT profile and device implementation are not verified.

TTA Part 4 — printed p.27 / PDF p.34

feature: Frequency-interleaver ceil bound and shift-register rule

ATSC.value: The symbol-offset generator uses 0 < k < ceil(L_FP/2), the N_r−1-bit shift assignment and the stated 8K/16K/32K XOR taps.
ATSC.req: normative algorithm for the selected interleaving mode

TTA.value: The corrected ceil(L_Fm/2) bound, shift and XOR-tap form are present despite the 2020 reference citation.

SBTVD.value: The referenced ATSC edition post-dates the 2021 correction. Full ABNT profile and the complete permutation output were not independently verified.

difference: The inspected corrected formula corresponds. This does not establish bit-exact equality of every interleaver output or other framing clauses.
impact: No discrepancy was found in this specific correction; implementation behavior remains untested.

TTA.text: Corrected bound, shift and listed XOR taps verified.

SBTVD.text: Referenced edition contains the correction; complete national profile not verified.

recommendation: Retain the scoped match and avoid using it as proof that all 2021 corrections or all of §7 were adopted.

feature: PLP limits, LDM and power-distribution tables

ATSC.value: Up to 64 PLPs and at most 4 PLPs composing a service; two-layer LDM is available, including defined combinations with MIMO/channel bonding. Tables 6.15 and 6.16 give power distributions and scaling/normalizing factors.
ATSC.req: PLP constraints; LDM is an optional technology with defined mode constraints

TTA.value: PLP limits and two-layer LDM correspond. Both power-distribution Table 6-15 and scaling/normalizing Table 6-16 are present (PDF pp.46–47); they must not be reported missing. Layered MIMO is described in I-1, whose non-normative declaration is retained. The cited rule requires at least one 4K UHD program in a 6 MHz multiplex.
TTA.req: LDM optional; national program-composition rule separate; I-1 not part of the standard

SBTVD.value: Decreto includes LDM in TV 3.0; Ato references A/322 for transmitter equipment. OG-01 describes LDM operation, relative robustness and injection level. Full normative receiver/mode support profile not verified.
SBTVD.req: system-level adoption by decree; transmitter rule; OG-01 non-normative

difference: The listed PLP/LDM technology is shared. Korean power-ratio tables are present. National requirements differ and do not by themselves prove every transmitter/receiver mode-support obligation.
impact: Multiplex design must respect the program-composition rule and the selected LDM/MIMO combinations. No deployed multiplex or receiver capability was inspected.

TTA.text: Listed PLP limits and LDM power-distribution/scaling tables correspond; complete combined-mode identity is not claimed.

SBTVD.text: Decree LDM adoption and OG-01 guidance verified; full ABNT normative mode/receiver profile remains open.

recommendation: Remove the false missing-table statement and cite Tables 6-15/6-16 explicitly. Verify ABNT receiver requirements before making blanket support claims.

feature: MIMO pilot tables: 32K MP4_2 correction, spacing and missing lookup entries

ATSC.value: Table L.9.2 gives D_x=6 for MP6_2/MP6_4 and includes MP24_2/MP24_4. Table L.9.3 allows only MP8_2 at 32K/GI6_1536; MP4_2 was removed because of a continual-pilot conflict.
ATSC.req: MIMO optional; permitted pilot combinations normative when used

TTA.value: Table I.10-4 prints D_x=3 for MP6_2/MP6_4 and omits MP24_2/MP24_4 from that lookup table, although MP24 patterns appear elsewhere. Table I.10-5 retains MP4_2 for 32K/GI6_1536 and has additional incomplete names (MP_4, M3_2, MP_2) differing from the current ATSC table. Appendix I-1 states it is not part of the standard.
TTA.req: MIMO optional; appendix declaration and printed discrepancies retained

SBTVD.doc: A/322:2025-07a by Ato reference · SBTVD OG-01
SBTVD.value: The regulatory reference precedes the January 2026 correction, but OG-01 explicitly prohibits MP4_2 with 32K FFT. It is therefore incorrect to say the reviewed Brazilian material simply leaves the combination available. Complete ABNT normative alignment remains unverified.
SBTVD.req: decree MIMO adoption; Ato transmitter requirement; OG-01 non-normative pilot restriction

difference: Korean table differences extend beyond the single MP4_2 entry. Brazil has an older regulatory reference and an explicit newer operating-guideline prohibition. Source typos shared by ATSC and TTA are not counted as national differences.
impact: Incorrect pilot spacing or an invalid pilot combination could prevent consistent implementations. No transmitter was shown to use the discrepant entries.
recommendation: Prepare explicit Korean table errata against current Tables L.9.2–L.9.4. Preserve Brazil’s Ato/ABNT/OG evidence separately and verify the normative profile rather than claiming the OG correction is absent.

TTA.text: Confirmed spacing, lookup-entry, pattern-name and stale MP4_2 differences.

SBTVD.text: OG-01 §5.13 already prohibits 32K MP4_2; older Ato reference and full ABNT normative alignment remain separate open items.

evidence.label: TTA Part 4 — Tables I.10-4/I.10-5, PDF p.326

feature: L1D_time_sec: current TAI meaning and the Korean worked-example discrepancy

ATSC.value: L1D_time_sec is the seconds portion of the precise TAI time at the first sample of the first symbol of the most recent bootstrap; it contains the 32 least significant seconds bits from the PTP epoch. The 2022 amendment also changed PTP/A/324 reference status.
ATSC.req: normative TAI interpretation; at least one time value per five-second interval

TTA.value: The older explanation remains and the worked example prints 17:31:48 UTC as equivalent to 17:31:24 TAI. This UTC value differs by 60 seconds from the ATSC worked example that gives the same TAI time and count 1455298284. The printed PDF was checked.
TTA.req: body definition and example require clarification/erratum; no device fault demonstrated

SBTVD.doc: A/322:2025-07a by reference · A/324:2025-07 by reference
SBTVD.value: The cited ATSC edition post-dates the 2022 clarification. No Brazil-specific time-definition deviation was identified in the reviewed guidelines; full ABNT normative text and time-chain behavior remain unverified.

difference: The current ATSC TAI clarification is material to the comparison and was not merely a reference-date change. The Korean worked example has an internal 60-second mismatch; this is not evidence of a measured broadcast delay.
impact: Ambiguous UTC/TAI examples can mislead implementation or measurement. Actual clocks, L1 timestamps and receiver interpretation require independent validation.
recommendation: Add the 2022 delta, propose correction of the Korean UTC example and keep printed-standard findings distinct from device timing measurements.

TTA.text: Older explanation and confirmed UTC worked-example discrepancy relative to current ATSC.

SBTVD.text: Referenced ATSC edition contains the clarification; complete national profile and implementation remain unverified.
